findings.observation: Frozen extensions.source_sha256 is {}, although source_files_to_pin names five files. execution_admission rejects any absent/empty expected map or any mismatched entry before require_gate.
findings.consequence: Even after authentication and a genuine matching root release become available, the unchanged F3 contract refuses before the shared gate and before panel/output creation.
findings.resolution_boundary: Root must arrange an additive prospective protocol version containing the exact five-file map, freeze it and bind any later release to its new hash. No frozen record was edited here.

findings.observation: Each frozen protocol declares a 120-second timeout/watchdog. F4 run.py and the identical F5/F7 panel_io.py contain a 2-GiB address-space guard but no signal timer, timed subprocess or other deadline. Their inspected launch recipes invoke Python directly and supply no external watchdog.
findings.consequence: The literal inspected recipe does not implement the frozen 120-second process guard. A later genuine release needs a concrete external supervisor that supplies it; none was executed or certified here.
findings.scope_limit: F2/F3 have 115-second panel alarms and F6/F8 have 112-second panel alarms after gate admission. These are not a demonstrated 120-second outer supervisor. F3/F6/F8 explicitly promise an external 120-second watchdog. No external launcher beyond the selected recipes was inspected.

findings.observation: execution.checkpoint declares application checkpoints every 60 seconds, grace 10 seconds and manifest_sha256 restore validation. The inspected runner has no periodic checkpoint timer, restore argument/path or restore-manifest validation, while extensions.checkpoint_detail and REPRODUCE say there is no in-place row resume and restored work uses a fresh attempt.
findings.consequence: Per-case JSON writes and the S3 pre-launch gate do not by themselves demonstrate the declared application checkpoint interval/grace/restore contract. A later release needs the intended semantics reconciled prospectively or a concrete external implementation identified.
findings.scope_limit: This is a mismatch between declared operational fields and the selected implementation, not an observed lost checkpoint, interrupted panel or mathematical result.

operational_notes.observation: The base-to-dispatch checkpoint.sh diff adds file_stat and replaces two stat invocations. It changes neither the gate subcommand nor the checkpoint_gate.require_gate signature. The common helper SHA-256 is 50359bb34063e97b6804c16e97624add872b0cc359df68776aacecc5e9e44039 and its bytes match de1f9bbe. checkpoint.sh is not in the selected frozen scientific source/input pin sets, so the stat-only operational repair does not itself trip those pins.
operational_notes.scope_limit: Static compatibility only. Neither the shell helper nor the real gate was invoked.

operational_notes.observation: F2/F4/F6/F8 default to their track-local phase-b-release.json; F3 uses track-local release.json; F5/F7 use runtime/releases/<TASK>.json. F5/F7 have no --protocol argument and always read track-local protocol.json. Other runners accept --protocol. Existing per-track recipes are compatible with these parser differences.
operational_notes.consequence: A single uniform --protocol argument or a single assumed release basename would break some tracks. Any later root command must follow the per-track contracts or explicitly pass the correct --release.

operational_notes.observation: F2/F4 enforce selected committed source/helper and interpreter identities before the gate. F3 would enforce its five-file map and interpreter after its map is completed. F5/F7 enforce selected track source and input bytes, then merely record the helper/interpreter hashes after the gate. F6/F8 record source/interpreter observations after the gate without comparing them to the frozen instrument commit/binary; they refuse -O. These latter contracts rely on the root pre-launch identity checks already required by RESUME.md.
operational_notes.consequence: The unchanged current bytes and interpreter match the pins. This inspection does not turn observation-only identity recording into a runtime refusal guard. Later release custody must retain actual byte and interpreter checks, including the common helper and operational checkpoint.sh revision.

operational_notes.observation: The common flock is held only while the real gate is called and its receipt read. It does not remain held during panels. The one-process worker limits and F5-then-F7/F6-then-F8 sequencing must therefore be supplied by later root scheduling.

The dispatch context says the user has now approved S3 disclosure, but the actual gate still fails because supported token/profile transport is missing and no experiment or release exists. This is supplied session context, not a gate/authentication observation by this inspection. The earlier RESUME.md and freeze archive still state disclosure consent is pending; those are historical records.
